subject: ShadowFax — VPC hosting constraints & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@shadowfax.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: ShadowFax — quick recap from this morning's VPC discussion

Aisha — thanks again for your time on the call this morning. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to capture the asks for your network/security team: 

Key pain points you shared:
- Data residency: ShadowFax must keep PII and model logs within US East (single-region requirement).
- Network egress restrictions: only outbound to a small allowlist of vendor IP ranges is allowed; NAT/proxy in DMZ is required for any external endpoint access.
- Air-gap preference for certain workloads: offline model packaging for regulated customers, with occasional controlled uploads via signed transfer window.

Goals you want solved by Redwood:
1) Host inference for internal and partner-facing features inside your VPC with clear residency guarantees.
2) Provide predictable latency for tier-1 flows (95th < 120ms for 512-token prompts).
3) Maintain audit trail and retention controls (logs retained 7 years for regulated customers).

Technical constraints noted:
- No inbound public IPs allowed on compute agents — must sit behind customer-managed NAT/load balancer.
- KMS integration mandatory (Cloud KMS with customer-managed keys).
- Shared storage limited to S3 buckets in the same region and restricted via endpoint policies.

Attachments we referenced:
- network-topology-sketch.png (sketch you shared)
- shadowfax-mop-diff.pdf (your draft MOP with highlighted constraints)

Immediate next steps (owner in parentheses):
- Ben: share a concise runbook for Redwood Private installation patterns that match your no-inbound-IP constraint (by EOD 4/27).
- Monica: produce a short checklist for our KMS and storage integration points and a proposal for audit-log export (by 4/30).
- Aisha: share your SOC/compliance contact and preferred vendor allowlist process (if available).

If I missed anything or misrepresented a constraint, say so and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll map a targeted engineering call next week to validate firewall rules and the signed transfer workflow.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0162

Subject: Re: ShadowFax — quick recap from this morning's VPC discussion

Thanks Ben — that summary looks correct. Adding a couple clarifications from our side: 

- The allowlist process is cross-functional; security will provide a signed CSV of allowed vendor IP ranges. Can Redwood accept both CIDR and single-IP entries?
- For the air-gap packaging: the offline bundle must be verifiable (checksum + signed manifest) and we will only allow uploads during established maintenance windows.
- Audit logs: Security requires immutable write-once logs; we use a combination of KMS-wrapped archives and a compliance S3 bucket with Object Lock enabled.

We’ll loop in Rajesh from Security (cc'ed) to validate the IP allowlist and object-lock expectations. Our preference is to run the validation call on 2027-04-29 (Thu) morning Eastern — does that work for your infra engineer?

Best,
Aisha Raman
Director, Product Security | ShadowFax Technologies
aisha.raman@shadowfax.com

Aisha / Rajesh — quick technical notes from our end before the validation call: 

- CIDR vs single-IP: Redwood Private accepts both; we will present a deployment where the serving layer makes outbound connections through customer-managed NAT. We will provide an allowlist template with both formats.
- KMS: we support Cloud KMS customer-managed keys; we will not persist plaintext keys on our side. We will provide a KMS integration checklist (KM/1) and an example IAM role.
- Object Lock: we can export immutable audit logs to your Object Lock–enabled bucket. We’ll include S3 ACL and bucket policy examples that meet write-once needs.
- Air-gap bundle: our packaging tool generates a signed manifest and SHA256 digest; we will add an extra signing step to match your signing keys if required.

Deliverables we’ll bring to the 4/29 validation call:
- Allowlist template (CSV + CIDR examples) — Monica (by 4/28)
- KMS and IAM role example — Vivek (by 4/28)
- Sample signed bundle flow and checklist for transfer windows — Monica (by 4/28)

Rajesh — please confirm preferred time on 4/29 and any additional artifacts you want us to prepare. If there are network engineers who prefer a separate deep-dive, we can schedule that the same day.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai

Thanks all — appreciate the quick alignment. Final confirmation items and timeline: 

1) Validation call: Thu 2027-04-29 10:00 AM ET (we'll send a calendar invite). Monica and Vivek will join to run through allowlist template, KMS examples, and signed-bundle flow. (Owner: Ben to schedule)
2) Deliverables due 4/28: allowlist_template.csv, KMS IAM example, sample bundle signing flow (Owners: Monica, Vivek)
3) ShadowFax to provide: security contact (Rajesh) and preliminary allowlist CSV if you can — otherwise security will provide during the validation call.

Risks we flagged:
- Latency SLOs: we need to validate RTT from your VPC subnets to our planned inference nodes. Monica will capture an RTT matrix during the engineering call.
- Transfer windows for air-gap uploads may add delay to your regulated feature releases; we’ll propose an SLO for inbound bundle ingestion (target < 4 business hours from signed upload).

If that looks correct I’ll lock the calendar invite and put the artifacts in the shared Drive link above. Looking forward to the validation call — please reply if the 4/29 time doesn't work.

Best,
